paragraphs.text: After these things Jesus manifested himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and he manifested [himself] on this wise.
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἐφανέρωσεν ἑαυτὸν πάλιν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης τῆς Τιβεριάδος· ἐφανέρωσεν δὲ οὕτως.
paragraphs.translit: Meta tauta ephanerōsen heauton palin ho Iēsous tois mathētais epi tēs thalassēs tēs Tiberiados· ephanerōsen de houtōs.

paragraphs.text: There was together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the [sons] of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν ὁμοῦ Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος καὶ Ναθαναὴλ ὁ ἀπὸ Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ οἱ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ ἄλλοι ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ δύο.
paragraphs.translit: ēsan homou Simōn Petros kai Thōmas ho legomenos Didymos kai Nathanaēl ho apo Kana tēs Galilaias kai hoi tou Zebedaiou kai alloi ek tōn mathētōn autou dyo.

paragraphs.text: Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also come with thee. They went forth, and entered into the boat; and that night they took nothing.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς Σίμων Πέτρος· Ὑπάγω ἁλιεύειν· λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἐρχόμεθα καὶ ἡμεῖς σὺν σοί. ἐξῆλθον καὶ ἐνέβησαν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ νυκτὶ ἐπίασαν οὐδέν.
paragraphs.translit: legei autois Simōn Petros· Hypagō halieuein· legousin autō· Erchometha kai hēmeis syn soi. exēlthon kai enebēsan eis to ploion, kai en ekeinē tē nykti epiasan ouden.

paragraphs.text: But when day was now breaking, Jesus stood on the beach: yet the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.
paragraphs.original: Πρωΐας δὲ ἤδη γενομένης ἔστη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸν αἰγιαλόν· οὐ μέντοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: Prōias de ēdē genomenēs estē Iēsous eis ton aigialon· ou mentoi ēdeisan hoi mathētai hoti Iēsous estin.

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore saith unto them, Children, have ye aught to eat? They answered him, No.
paragraphs.original: λέγει οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Παιδία, μή τι προσφάγιον ἔχετε; ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ· Οὔ.
paragraphs.translit: legei oun autois ho Iēsous· Paidia, mē ti prosphagion echete; apekrithēsan autō· Ou.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Βάλετε εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τοῦ πλοίου τὸ δίκτυον, καὶ εὑρήσετε. ἔβαλον οὖν, καὶ οὐκέτι αὐτὸ ἑλκύσαι ἴσχυον ἀπὸ τοῦ πλήθους τῶν ἰχθύων.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· Balete eis ta dexia merē tou ploiou to diktyon, kai heurēsete. ebalon oun, kai ouketi auto helkysai ischyon apo tou plēthous tōn ichthyōn.

paragraphs.text: That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved saith unto Peter, It is the Lord. So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his coat about him (for he was naked), and cast himself into the sea.
paragraphs.original: λέγει οὖν ὁ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ὁ κύριός ἐστιν. Σίμων οὖν Πέτρος, ἀκούσας ὅτι ὁ κύριός ἐστιν, τὸν ἐπενδύτην διεζώσατο, ἦν γὰρ γυμνός, καὶ ἔβαλεν ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν·
paragraphs.translit: legei oun ho mathētēs ekeinos hon ēgapa ho Iēsous tō Petrō· Ho kyrios estin. Simōn oun Petros, akousas hoti ho kyrios estin, ton ependytēn diezōsato, ēn gar gymnos, kai ebalen heauton eis tēn thalassan·

paragraphs.text: But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits off), dragging the net [full] of fishes.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἄλλοι μαθηταὶ τῷ πλοιαρίῳ ἦλθον, οὐ γὰρ ἦσαν μακρὰν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀλλὰ ὡς ἀπὸ πηχῶν διακοσίων, σύροντες τὸ δίκτυον τῶν ἰχθύων.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de alloi mathētai tō ploiariō ēlthon, ou gar ēsan makran apo tēs gēs alla hōs apo pēchōn diakosiōn, syrontes to diktyon tōn ichthyōn.

paragraphs.text: So when they got out upon the land, they see a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread.
paragraphs.original: Ὡς οὖν ἀπέβησαν εἰς τὴν γῆν βλέπουσιν ἀνθρακιὰν κειμένην καὶ ὀψάριον ἐπικείμενον καὶ ἄρτον.
paragraphs.translit: Hōs oun apebēsan eis tēn gēn blepousin anthrakian keimenēn kai opsarion epikeimenon kai arton.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto them, Bring of the fish which ye have now taken.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐνέγκατε ἀπὸ τῶν ὀψαρίων ὧν ἐπιάσατε νῦν.
paragraphs.translit: legei autois ho Iēsous· Enenkate apo tōn opsariōn hōn epiasate nyn.

paragraphs.text: Simon Peter therefore went up, and drew the net to land, full of great fishes, a hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, the net was not rent.
paragraphs.original: ἀνέβη οὖν Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ εἵλκυσεν τὸ δίκτυον εἰς τὴν γῆν μεστὸν ἰχθύων μεγάλων ἑκατὸν πεντήκοντα τριῶν· καὶ τοσούτων ὄντων οὐκ ἐσχίσθη τὸ δίκτυον.
paragraphs.translit: anebē oun Simōn Petros kai heilkysen to diktyon eis tēn gēn meston ichthyōn megalōn hekaton pentēkonta triōn· kai tosoutōn ontōn ouk eschisthē to diktyon.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto them, Come [and] break your fast. And none of the disciples durst inquire of him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Δεῦτε ἀριστήσατε. οὐδεὶς δὲ ἐτόλμα τῶν μαθητῶν ἐξετάσαι αὐτόν· Σὺ τίς εἶ; εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ κύριός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: legei autois ho Iēsous· Deute aristēsate. oudeis de etolma tōn mathētōn exetasai auton· Sy tis ei; eidotes hoti ho kyrios estin.

paragraphs.text: Jesus cometh, and taketh the bread, and giveth them, and the fish likewise.
paragraphs.original: ἔρχεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ λαμβάνει τὸν ἄρτον καὶ δίδωσιν αὐτοῖς, καὶ τὸ ὀψάριον ὁμοίως.
paragraphs.translit: erchetai ho Iēsous kai lambanei ton arton kai didōsin autois, kai to opsarion homoiōs.

paragraphs.text: This is now the third time that Jesus was manifested to the disciples, after that he was risen from the dead.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο ἤδη τρίτον ἐφανερώθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: touto ēdē triton ephanerōthē ho Iēsous tois mathētais egertheis ek nekrōn.

paragraphs.text: So when they had broken their fast, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, [son] of John, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
paragraphs.original: Ὅτε οὖν ἠρίστησαν λέγει τῷ Σίμωνι Πέτρῳ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Σίμων Ἰωάννου, ἀγαπᾷς με πλέον τούτων; λέγει αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε, σὺ οἶδας ὅτι φιλῶ σε. λέγει αὐτῷ· Βόσκε τὰ ἀρνία μου.
paragraphs.translit: Hote oun ēristēsan legei tō Simōni Petrō ho Iēsous· Simōn Iōannou, agapas me pleon toutōn; legei autō· Nai, kyrie, sy oidas hoti philō se. legei autō· Boske ta arnia mou.

paragraphs.text: He saith to him again a second time, Simon, [son] of John, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Tend my sheep.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ πάλιν δεύτερον· Σίμων Ἰωάννου, ἀγαπᾷς με; λέγει αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε, σὺ οἶδας ὅτι φιλῶ σε. λέγει αὐτῷ· Ποίμαινε τὰ πρόβατά μου.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō palin deuteron· Simōn Iōannou, agapas me; legei autō· Nai, kyrie, sy oidas hoti philō se. legei autō· Poimaine ta probata mou.

paragraphs.text: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, [son] of John, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ τὸ τρίτον· Σίμων Ἰωάννου, φιλεῖς με; ἐλυπήθη ὁ Πέτρος ὅτι εἶπεν αὐτῷ τὸ τρίτον· Φιλεῖς με; καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, πάντα σὺ οἶδας, σὺ γινώσκεις ὅτι φιλῶ σε. λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Βόσκε τὰ πρόβατά μου.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō to triton· Simōn Iōannou, phileis me; elypēthē ho Petros hoti eipen autō to triton· Phileis me; kai eipen autō· Kyrie, panta sy oidas, sy ginōskeis hoti philō se. legei autō ho Iēsous· Boske ta probata mou.

paragraphs.text: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, ὅτε ἦς νεώτερος, ἐζώννυες σεαυτὸν καὶ περιεπάτεις ὅπου ἤθελες· ὅταν δὲ γηράσῃς, ἐκτενεῖς τὰς χεῖράς σου, καὶ ἄλλος σε ζώσει καὶ οἴσει ὅπου οὐ θέλεις.
paragraphs.translit: amēn amēn legō soi, hote ēs neōteros, ezōnnyes seauton kai periepateis hopou ētheles· hotan de gērasēs, ekteneis tas cheiras sou, kai allos se zōsei kai oisei hopou ou theleis.

paragraphs.text: Now this he spake, signifying by what manner of death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ εἶπεν σημαίνων ποίῳ θανάτῳ δοξάσει τὸν θεόν. καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι.
paragraphs.translit: touto de eipen sēmainōn poiō thanatō doxasei ton theon. kai touto eipōn legei autō· Akolouthei moi.

paragraphs.text: Peter, turning about, seeth the disciple whom Jesus loved following; who also leaned back on his breast at the supper, and said, Lord, who is he that betrayeth thee?
paragraphs.original: Ἐπιστραφεὶς ὁ Πέτρος βλέπει τὸν μαθητὴν ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀκολουθοῦντα, ὃς καὶ ἀνέπεσεν ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν· Κύριε, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παραδιδούς σε;
paragraphs.translit: Epistrapheis ho Petros blepei ton mathētēn hon ēgapa ho Iēsous akolouthounta, hos kai anepesen en tō deipnō epi to stēthos autou kai eipen· Kyrie, tis estin ho paradidous se;

paragraphs.text: Peter therefore seeing him saith to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do?
paragraphs.original: τοῦτον οὖν ἰδὼν ὁ Πέτρος λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Κύριε, οὗτος δὲ τί;
paragraphs.translit: touton oun idōn ho Petros legei tō Iēsou· Kyrie, houtos de ti;

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what [is that] to thee? Follow thou me.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐὰν αὐτὸν θέλω μένειν ἕως ἔρχομαι, τί πρὸς σέ; σύ μοι ἀκολούθει.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō ho Iēsous· Ean auton thelō menein heōs erchomai, ti pros se; sy moi akolouthei.

paragraphs.text: This saying therefore went forth among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, that he should not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what [is that] to thee?
paragraphs.original: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν οὗτος ὁ λόγος εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι ὁ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος οὐκ ἀποθνῄσκει. οὐκ εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι οὐκ ἀποθνῄσκει ἀλλʼ· Ἐὰν αὐτὸν θέλω μένειν ἕως ἔρχομαι, τί πρὸς σέ;
paragraphs.translit: exēlthen oun houtos ho logos eis tous adelphous hoti ho mathētēs ekeinos ouk apothnēskei. ouk eipen de autō ho Iēsous hoti ouk apothnēskei allʼ· Ean auton thelō menein heōs erchomai, ti pros se;

paragraphs.text: This is the disciple that beareth witness of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his witness is true.
paragraphs.original: Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ μαθητὴς ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ τούτων καὶ ὁ γράψας ταῦτα, καὶ οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς αὐτοῦ ἡ μαρτυρία ἐστίν.
paragraphs.translit: Houtos estin ho mathētēs ho martyrōn peri toutōn kai ho grapsas tauta, kai oidamen hoti alēthēs autou hē martyria estin.

paragraphs.text: And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself would not contain the books that should be written.
paragraphs.original: ἔστιν δὲ καὶ ἄλλα πολλὰ ἃ ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἅτινα ἐὰν γράφηται καθʼ ἕν, οὐδʼ αὐτὸν οἶμαι τὸν κόσμον χωρήσειν τὰ γραφόμενα βιβλία.
paragraphs.translit: estin de kai alla polla ha epoiēsen ho Iēsous, hatina ean graphētai kathʼ hen, oudʼ auton oimai ton kosmon chōrēsein ta graphomena biblia.
